title: Outfinitism
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: The target improved, the care did not
scenes.viewerPurpose: Measured success can differ from lived improvement. Proposes a philosophy of limits on the authority of models, linking explicit boundaries to practical rights of correction and action.
scenes.composition: Keep an improved waiting-time measure beside a patient whose care has not improved. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Keep an improved waiting-time measure beside a patient whose care has not improved.
Show the measure’s frame without allowing it to cover the whole care scene.

cues.text: A hospital reduces its measured waiting time while the care people receive gets worse.
cues.visualAction: Keep an improved waiting-time measure beside a patient whose care has not improved.
cues.emotion: Sober recognition; gently emphasize “care gets worse”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: Outfinitism argues that useful models become dangerous when their chosen measurements start deciding what counts as real.
cues.visualAction: Show the measure’s frame without allowing it to cover the whole care scene.
cues.emotion: Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “what counts as real”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.

scenes.title: What the model left outside
scenes.viewerPurpose: A useful model can exceed its scope. The philosophy addresses knowledge and power.
scenes.composition: Let the selected variables grow in prominence while an important lived detail remains outside them. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.

cues.text: The book explores how useful models gain power until their chosen measurements seem to describe everything.
cues.visualAction: Let the selected variables grow in prominence while an important lived detail remains outside them.

cues.text: It brings science, institutions, and AI together to ask where knowledge and authority need limits.

scenes.title: Correction that changes something
scenes.viewerPurpose: Complexity cannot excuse endless hesitation. Limits need practical effects.
scenes.composition: Hold two relevant viewpoints beside a decision that still must be made. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.

cues.visualAction: Hold two relevant viewpoints beside a decision that still must be made.

cues.text: The inquiry asks how these limits could change what people can question, correct, or do.

scenes.viewerPurpose: The challenge applies to the viewer’s own certainty. The opening returns the target to human experience.
